itens.titulo: CVE-2026-129448: Apache Roller Deserialization of Untrusted Data Vulnerability
itens.resumo: Apache Roller contains a deserialization of untrusted data vulnerability that allows an unauthenticated remote attacker to execute arbitrary code via the XML-RPC endpoint, which accepts and deserializes vendor extension types before authentication. This CVE covers the same underlying vulnerability as CVE-2026-82384 but applies to a broader range of affected versions.

itens.titulo: CVE-2026-123890: VMWare vCenter Authentication Bypass Using an Alternate Path or Channel Vulnerability
itens.resumo: Broadcom VMware vCenter contains an authentication bypass using an alternate path or channel vulnerability in the VMware Directory Service that allows an unauthenticated attacker with network access to vCenter to bypass authentication and gain unauthorized access to the system.

itens.titulo: CVE-2025-42884: SAP NetWeaver Improper Neutralization of Special Elements in Data Query Logic Vulnerability
itens.resumo: SAP NetWeaver Enterprise Portal contains an improper neutralization of special elements in data query logic vulnerability that allows an unauthenticated attacker to disclose or modify server information via injected JNDI environment properties or a URL used during JNDI lookup operations.

itens.titulo: CVE-2026-76466: Cisco Expressway Series Use of Hard-coded Credentials Vulnerability
itens.resumo: Cisco Expressway Series contains a use of hard-coded credentials vulnerability that allows an unauthenticated, remote attacker with persistent cookies and network access to execute commands as root on a clustered device via the database service.

itens.titulo: CTO of ‘RansomwareHelp’ Indicted for Wire Fraud
itens.resumo: The chief technology officer and co-founder of ransomwarehelp.com, a six year old Florida business that claimed to use "advanced cryptographic tools" to restore data locked by ransomware, has been charged with wire fraud after an FBI sting operation found the company was simply paying the attackers for a decryption key and charging victims a markup for work that was never performed.

itens.titulo: GnuPG Warns Critical GPGME Flaw Could Expose App Data via Malicious OpenPGP Keys
itens.resumo: A malicious OpenPGP key with an unusually long user ID can trigger a critical memory bug in GPGME, the standard library that programs use to work with GnuPG. The GnuPG project warned yesterday that the flaw could be used to steal data from affected applications and has released fixed versions.
